text:
Formalized in 2001 by the NINDS Stroke Progress Review Group, the neurovascular unit (NVU) concept emphasizes the intimate brain–vessel relationship. Evidence supports a conceptual shift in neurovascular coupling: from a unidimensional neuronal–astrocytic signaling process to a multidimensional one in which mediators from multiple cells engage distinct pathways and effector systems across the cerebrovascular network in a highly orchestrated manner. Recently appreciated NVU dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases supports emerging concepts that maintaining neurovascular health promotes brain health.

In COPD, smokers showed increased neutrophils and CD8+ cells within airway smooth muscle versus non-smokers, suggesting these cells drive smoking-induced airflow limitation. Immunohistochemistry of 26 thoracotomy specimens (8 COPD smokers, 10 smokers with normal lung function, 8 non-smoking controls) quantified neutrophils, macrophages, mast cells, and CD4+/CD8+ cells. Smokers with normal lung function also showed neutrophilic infiltration. Neutrophilic infiltration was inversely related to FEV1 (% predicted). Neutrophil and CD8+ microlocalisation implicates them in pathogenesis.
